- Overestimate prices when sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.8) in recent days, especially after spikes; reduce forecast peak by 5–15%.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is strongly bearish (≤-0.5) or shows sudden reversal; add 3–8% to forecast to avoid bottoming too early.
- Model tends to overshoot after sharp upward moves; apply a 1–3 day lag correction by reducing forecast by 2–5% for the next 3–5 days post-spike.
- Mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show downward trend + negative sentiment, forecast should trend lower by 1–3% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
- For 30-day horizon, avoid overfitting to recent highs; if last 5 days are above 70, cap forecast at 70–72 unless sentiment is strong bullish.
- When sentiment is neutral (0.2–0.6) and price is volatile, reduce forecast variance by 10–20% to avoid overconfidence in short-term momentum.
